section_title: Mendel and His Work on Inheritance
prompt:
# Segment 1 (0-14.2s) - Introduction to Mendel
title = Text("Gregor Johann Mendel", font_size=48).to_edge(UP)
subtitle = Text("Father of Genetics", font_size=36).next_to(title, DOWN)

bullet_points1 = VGroup(
    Text("• Conducted experiments on plant breeding", font_size=32),
    Text("• Proposed laws of inheritance", font_size=32),
    Text("• Selected Plant: Pisum sativum (garden pea)", font_size=32)
).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).move_to(ORIGIN)

self.play(Write(title), run_time=2)
self.play(FadeIn(subtitle), run_time=2)
self.play(Create(bullet_points1), run_time=4)
self.wait(6.2)

# Segment 2 (14.2-36.0s) - Contrasting Characters
self.play(FadeOut(bullet_points1), run_time=1)

table_title = Text("Contrasting Characters", font_size=36).to_edge(UP)
headers = VGroup(
    Text("Character", font_size=28),
    Text("Dominant", font_size=28),
    Text("Recessive", font_size=28)
).arrange(RIGHT, buff=1).next_to(table_title, DOWN)

traits = [
    ["Flower colour", "Violet", "White"],
    ["Seed colour", "Yellow", "Green"],
    ["Seed shape", "Round", "Wrinkled"],
    ["Height", "Tall", "Dwarf"]
]

table_rows = VGroup()
for trait in traits:
    row = VGroup(
        Text(trait[0], font_size=24),
        Text(trait[1], font_size=24),
        Text(trait[2], font_size=24)
    ).arrange(RIGHT, buff=1)
    table_rows.add(row)
table_rows.arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).next_to(headers, DOWN)

self.play(Write(table_title), run_time=2)
self.play(Create(headers), run_time=2)
self.play(Create(table_rows), run_time=8)
self.wait(8.8)

# Segment 3 (36.0-57.4s) - Inheritance Ratios
self.play(FadeOut(table_title), FadeOut(headers), FadeOut(table_rows), run_time=1)

mono_title = Text("Monohybrid Cross (F2)", font_size=36).to_edge(UP)
mono_ratio = MathTex(r"3:1").scale(2).next_to(mono_title, DOWN)

di_title = Text("Dihybrid Cross (F2)", font_size=36).next_to(mono_ratio, DOWN, buff=1)
di_ratio = MathTex(r"9:3:3:1").scale(2).next_to(di_title, DOWN)

self.play(Write(mono_title), run_time=2)
self.play(Write(mono_ratio), run_time=2)
self.play(Write(di_title), run_time=2)
self.play(Write(di_ratio), run_time=2)
self.wait(13.3)

# Segment 4 (57.4-72.1s) - Mendel's Conclusions
self.play(FadeOut(mono_title), FadeOut(mono_ratio), 
          FadeOut(di_title), FadeOut(di_ratio), run_time=1)

conclusions_title = Text("Mendel's Conclusions:", font_size=40).to_edge(UP)
conclusions = VGroup(
    Text("• Traits show dominance and recessiveness", font_size=32),
    Text("• Law of Segregation", font_size=32),
    Text("• Law of Independent Assortment", font_size=32)
).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).move_to(ORIGIN)

self.play(Write(conclusions_title), run_time=2)
self.play(Create(conclusions), run_time=4)
self.wait(7.7)

# Segment 5 (72.1-92.9s) - Genes and Proteins
self.play(FadeOut(conclusions_title), FadeOut(conclusions), run_time=1)

final_text = VGroup(
    Text("Genes", font_size=36),
    Arrow(LEFT, RIGHT, color=WHITE),
    Text("Proteins", font_size=36),
    Arrow(LEFT, RIGHT, color=WHITE),
    Text("Traits", font_size=36)
).arrange(RIGHT).move_to(ORIGIN)

inheritance = Text("One allele from each parent", font_size=32).next_to(final_text, DOWN, buff=1)

self.play(Create(final_text), run_time=4)
self.play(Write(inheritance), run_time=3)
self.wait(12.8)

Cinematic 3D animation visualizing human sex determination. The scene begins showing a vast number of sperm cells swimming towards a large, glowing ovum. Half the sperm are highlighted with a blue 'Y' chromosome, and the other half with a pink 'X'. The camera follows one 'Y' sperm as it successfully penetrates the ovum, which contains a visible pink 'X' chromosome. Upon fertilization, the two chromosomes fuse, creating a zygote with a visible 'XY' pair. The scene then transitions to show an alternative outcome, where an 'X' sperm fertilizes the egg, resulting in an 'XX' zygote. The final shot splits the screen, showing the 'XY' zygote developing into a male embryo on one side and the 'XX' zygote into a female embryo on the other, clearly illustrating the 50% probability.

A cinematic, slow-motion shot of Gregor Mendel, a gentle, thoughtful man in 19th-century attire, walking through a sun-drenched monastery garden. He is carefully examining pea plants, gently touching a vibrant violet flower on one plant and then a white flower on another. The camera focuses on his notebook where he is meticulously recording his observations with a quill pen. The lighting is soft and golden, evoking a sense of historical discovery and scientific curiosity. The background is filled with rows of lush green pea plants, creating a serene and focused atmosphere. Duration: 12 seconds.

An abstract, stylized 3D animation inside a cell nucleus. We see a pair of homologous chromosomes, visualized as elegant, intertwining light structures. The camera zooms into a specific location, or locus, on the chromosomes. Here, two alleles for flower color appear as glowing symbols: a capital 'W' for the dominant violet trait on one chromosome and a lowercase 'w' for the recessive white trait on the other. The dominant 'W' allele pulses with a brighter light, visually overpowering the dimmer 'w' allele, symbolizing the concept of dominance in a clear, metaphorical way. The background is dark and cosmic, emphasizing the genetic code. Duration: 12 seconds.

A dynamic and clean animation of a Punnett square for a monohybrid cross. The screen starts with the parent genotypes 'Tt' and 'Tt' at the top and side of a 2x2 grid. Gametes 'T' and 't' slide into place along the axes. Then, the four squares of the grid fill in one by one in a satisfying sequence: 'TT', 'Tt', 'Tt', 'tt'. As each square fills, a small icon of a tall or short pea plant appears within it. Finally, the results are tallied at the bottom of the screen, with text appearing: 'Genotypic Ratio: 1 TT : 2 Tt : 1 tt' and 'Phenotypic Ratio: 3 Tall : 1 Short'. The animation uses a clean, modern graphic style with a white background and bold, colorful text. Duration: 12 seconds.

A clear, educational animation showing the chromosomal basis of sex determination in humans. The screen is split. On the left, a male figure with 'XY' chromosomes shown in his cells. On the right, a female figure with 'XX' chromosomes. Animated arrows show the process of meiosis, where the male produces sperm cells containing either an 'X' or a 'Y' chromosome, and the female produces egg cells all containing an 'X'. The gametes then move to the center and combine in two possible ways: X-sperm + X-egg results in an 'XX' zygote (female), and Y-sperm + X-egg results in an 'XY' zygote (male), with a 50% probability displayed for each outcome. The visual style is simple, using clear icons and diagrams against a neutral background. Duration: 12 seconds.

A heartwarming and uplifting montage of diverse Indian faces. The camera smoothly pans and cuts between close-up portraits of men, women, and children of different ages and backgrounds. The focus is on the beautiful variety of inherited traits: different eye colors (brown, black, hazel), skin tones, hair textures (straight, curly, wavy), and facial features. Everyone is smiling, looking directly at the camera. The video is shot with warm, natural lighting and a shallow depth of field, creating a personal and connected feel. The final shot is a group of friends laughing together, celebrating the diversity that makes humanity unique. Duration: 12 seconds.
